cards.heading: Three loops of agentic development
cards.question: What are the three nested feedback loops in Andrew Ng's framework for AI-assisted product building, and at what cadence does each close?
cards.answer: Agentic coding loop (minutes) — agent codes, tests, fixes against spec/evals; developer feedback loop (tens of minutes to hours) — human reviews and re-steers; external feedback loop (hours to weeks) — real users reshape the product vision.

cards.heading: How the three loops feed each other
cards.question: In what direction does information flow between the three loops?
cards.answer: Outside-in: external feedback informs the developer's vision, the vision becomes spec and steering for the agent, and the agent's self-testing loop turns spec into working software.

cards.heading: Effect of closing the inner loop
cards.question: What changed for developers once agents could test their own work, including driving a browser against what they built?
cards.answer: It moved developers out of the manual-QA role, freeing their time for product decisions.

cards.heading: When to invest in evals
cards.question: What signal indicates it's time to write evals for the agentic coding loop?
cards.answer: Recurring agent failures on the same problem.

cards.heading: Why the developer loop resists automation
cards.question: According to Ng, why does the middle (developer feedback) loop resist automation, and what explanation does he explicitly reject?
cards.answer: He rejects taste as the explanation; instead the human has a context advantage — knowledge of users and environment that the AI lacks — so a human-in-the-loop is needed as long as that knowledge gap exists.

cards.heading: Consequence: engineers as PMs
cards.question: As agents absorb implementation work, what shift does Ng predict for engineers?
cards.answer: Engineers increasingly take on product-management work, balancing building against gathering the user feedback that evolves the product vision.
